title: Africa 6 of 8 · East Africa and Great Lakes
edition: Africa countries · Eight regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Africa episode six of eight. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
Five countries connect the Great Lakes with the Indian Ocean: Uganda, Kenya, Rwanda, Burundi and Tanzania. This shorter lesson gives extra attention to the small inland pair.

states.name: Uganda
lines: Uganda is landlocked west of Kenya and north of Tanzania and Rwanda. Its southern side reaches Lake Victoria, while the Democratic Republic of the Congo lies west.
Bwindi’s forest in southwestern Uganda is habitat for mountain gorillas. The protected landscape lies where lowland and mountain forests meet, supporting rich plant and animal life.
Picture a gorilla forest west of Kenya and above Lake Victoria. Uganda has a great lake shore but no ocean coastline.
states.transition: Let's bring Uganda and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Kenya
lines: Kenya lies east of Uganda, below Ethiopia and Somalia, and above Tanzania. Its southeastern coastline reaches the Indian Ocean.
The Great Rift Valley lakes in Kenya support remarkable birdlife, including large gatherings of flamingos. Different lake conditions create feeding places for different species.
Remember pink birds along the rift, with the Indian Ocean beyond the southeast. Kenya is the coastal neighbour east of Uganda and north of Tanzania.

states.name: Rwanda
lines: Rwanda is the small landlocked country below Uganda, east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and above Burundi. Tanzania borders its eastern side.
Nyungwe National Park preserves montane rainforest with chimpanzees and other primates. Mountain forest is an important part of this country’s landscape, despite its small area.
Picture a forested highland patch above Burundi. Keep the small pair in order: Rwanda north, Burundi south, both inland west of Tanzania.
states.transition: Let's bring Rwanda and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Burundi
lines: Burundi lies immediately below Rwanda, east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and west of Tanzania. Its southwestern edge reaches Lake Tanganyika.
The ritual dance of the royal drum combines powerful ensemble drumming with dance and song. This living cultural tradition makes the drum a memorable symbol for Burundi.
Hear the drum below Rwanda and beside Lake Tanganyika. Burundi is the southern member of the small inland pair; neither country reaches the ocean.

states.name: Tanzania
lines: Tanzania lies below Kenya and Uganda, east of Rwanda and Burundi, and north of Mozambique. It reaches the Indian Ocean and includes Zanzibar offshore.
On the Serengeti plains, great herds of wildebeest, zebras and gazelles move in search of water and grazing. Predators follow this seasonal movement across the wider ecosystem.
Picture moving herds below Kenya, with Zanzibar offshore to the east. Tanzania connects the Great Lakes region with the Indian Ocean coast.
states.transition: Let's bring Tanzania and its neighbours into view.

recap: Uganda lies west of Kenya and above Lake Victoria. Rwanda is above Burundi, both west of Tanzania. Tanzania lies below Kenya and reaches the Indian Ocean, with Zanzibar offshore.

Recall Uganda’s gorilla forest, Kenya’s rift-lake birds, Rwanda’s mountain forest, Burundi’s drums and Tanzania’s moving herds. Great lakes give inland countries shores, but those are not ocean coastlines.
